label: Sample Exam Set C
source: ISTQB CTFL v4.0 Sample Exam C, Questions v1.6 / Answers v1.6 (istqb.org)

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical test objective?
o: Validating that documented requirements are met
Initiating errors and identifying root causes
Verifying the test object meets user expectations
questions.e: Causing failures and identifying defects is the most common objective of dynamic testing. Checking documented requirements is verification, identifying root causes belongs to debugging, and judging whether the object meets user expectations is validation, not verification.

questions.q: Which of the following statements BEST describes the difference between testing and debugging?
o: Testing causes failures while debugging fixes failures
Testing is a negative activity while debugging is a positive activity
Testing determines that defects exist while debugging removes defects
Testing finds the cause of defects while debugging fixes the cause of defects
questions.e: Testing shows that defects exist, directly in reviews or indirectly through failures, while debugging is the separate activity that locates and fixes defects. Debugging does not fix failures or the human errors behind defects.

questions.q: The 'absence-of-defects fallacy' is one of the principles of testing. Which of the following is an example of addressing this principle in practice?
o: Explaining that it is not possible for testing to show the absence of defects
Supporting the end users to perform acceptance testing
Ensuring that no implementation defects remain in the delivered system
Modifying tests that cause no failures to ensure few defects remain
questions.e: The fallacy is that fixing every defect guarantees user satisfaction, so its remedy is validating that needs and expectations are met, for example through acceptance testing with end users. Explaining untestability and modifying stale tests address other principles.

questions.q: Which of the following test activities are MOST likely to involve the application of boundary value analysis and equivalence partitioning?
questions.e: Test techniques are applied in test analysis to identify test conditions and coverage items, and in test design to create test cases from them. Implementation assembles procedures, execution runs them, and monitoring compares progress with the plan.

questions.q:
Match the testware (1-4) with the test activities that produce it (A-D):
1. Coverage items
2. Change requests
3. Test execution schedule
4. Prioritized test conditions
A. Test analysis
B. Test design
C. Test implementation
D. Test completion
questions.e: Test analysis produces prioritized test conditions (4A), test design produces coverage items (1B), test implementation produces the test execution schedule (3C), and test completion produces change requests and lessons learned (2D).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the different testing roles is MOST likely to be CORRECT?
o: In Agile software development, the test management role is the primary responsibility of the team, while the testing role is primarily the responsibility of a single individual from outside the team
The testing role is primarily responsible for test monitoring and test control, while the test management role is primarily responsible for test planning and test completion
In Agile software development, test management activities that span multiple teams are handled by a test manager outside the team, while some test management tasks are handled by the team itself
The test management role is primarily responsible for test analysis and test design, while the testing role is primarily responsible for test implementation and test execution
questions.e: An agile team handles many test management tasks itself, while test management spanning several teams is handled by a test manager outside the team. The test management role covers planning, monitoring, control and completion, and the testing role covers analysis, design, implementation and execution.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole-team approach?
questions.e: Using everyone's skills effectively improves team dynamics, communication and collaboration, creating a synergy that benefits the whole project. The approach has no rule about team size and does not remove the need for testing expertise.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the independence of testing is CORRECT?
o: Independent testers will find defects due to their different technical perspective from developers, but their independence may lead to an adversarial relationship with the developers
Developers' familiarity with their own code means they only find a few defects in it, however their shared software background with testers means these defects would also be found by the testers
Independent testing requires testers who are outside the developer's team and ideally from outside the organization, however these testers find it difficult to understand the application domain
Testers from outside the developer's team are more independent than testers from within the team, but the testers from within the team are more likely to be blamed for delays in product release
questions.e: Different perspectives and biases let independent testers find defects that developers miss, but independence risks isolation, poor collaboration and an adversarial relationship. Independence comes in levels and does not require testers from outside the organization.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
o: For each test level, there is a corresponding development level
For each test objective, there is a corresponding development objective
For every test activity, there is a corresponding user activity
For every development activity, there is a corresponding test activity
questions.e: Quality control applies to every development activity, so each development activity has a corresponding test activity. There is no such symmetry for development levels, development objectives or user activities.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?
questions.e: Acceptance Test-Driven Development is a well-known test-first approach. The other three names do not describe real test-first practices.

questions.q: Which of the following provides the BEST description of shift-left?
o: When agreed by the developers, manual activities on the left-hand side of the test process are automated to support the principle of 'early testing saves time and money'
Where cost-effective, test activities are moved earlier in the software development lifecycle (SDLC) to reduce the total cost of quality by reducing the number of defects found later in the SDLC
When they have spare time available, testers are required to automate tests for regression testing, starting with component tests and component integration tests
When available, testers are trained to perform tasks early in the SDLC to allow more test activities to be automated later in the SDLC
questions.e: Shift-left moves cost-effective test activities earlier in the SDLC so fewer defects survive into later phases, reducing total cost of quality. Automating later activities or automating regression suites is not shift-left.

questions.q: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur as a result of a retrospective?
o: The quality of future test objects improves by identifying improvements in development practices
Test efficiency improves by speeding up the configuration of test environments through automation
End users' understanding of the development and test processes is improved
Automated test scripts are enhanced through feedback from developers
questions.e: Retrospectives involve testers, developers, architects, product owners and analysts; end users are rarely present and do not receive their output, so their understanding is unlikely to improve. The other three outcomes are typical retrospective benefits.

questions.q: Which of the following test levels is MOST likely being performed if the testing is focused on validation and is not being performed by testers?
questions.e: Acceptance testing validates that the system meets business needs and is ideally carried out by end users. Component, component integration and system integration testing are mostly verification performed by developers or testers.

questions.q: The navigation system software has been updated due to it suggesting routes that break traffic laws, such as driving the wrong way down one-way streets. Which of the following BEST describes the testing that will be performed?
questions.e: First confirmation testing checks that the update really fixes the defect, then regression testing checks that no defects were introduced or uncovered in unchanged areas. When an update is tested, confirmation precedes regression.

questions.q:
Which of the following example defects could be found by static testing rather than dynamic testing?
i. Two different parts of the design specification disagree due to the complexity of the design
ii. A response time is too long and so makes users lose patience
iii. A path in the code cannot be reached during execution
iv. A variable is declared but never subsequently used in the program
v. The amount of memory needed by the program to generate a report is too high
questions.e: Specification inconsistencies (i), unreachable code (iii) and unused variables (iv) are defects that reviews and static analysis find most easily. Response time and memory consumption can only be measured by executing the program.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback?
o: Changes to requirements are understood and implemented earlier
It ensures business stakeholders understand user requirements
It allows product owners to change their requirements as often as they want
End users are told which requirements will not be implemented prior to release
questions.e: Early and frequent feedback lets the team understand and implement changed requirements sooner and prevents misunderstandings. It does not encourage unlimited change, and it is feedback from stakeholders, not to them.

questions.q:
Match the review types (1-4) with the descriptions (A-D):
1. Technical review
2. Informal review
3. Inspection
4. Walkthrough
A. Includes objectives such as gaining consensus, generating new ideas, and motivating authors to improve
B. Includes objectives such as educating reviewers, gaining consensus, generating new ideas and detecting potential defects
C. The main objective is detecting potential defects and it requires metrics collection to support process improvement
D. The main objective is detecting potential defects and it generates no formal documented output
questions.e: A technical review is led by a moderator and seeks consensus and new ideas (1A), an informal review mainly detects anomalies with no formal output (2D), an inspection is the most formal type and collects metrics (3C), and a walkthrough, led by the author, educates reviewers and detects defects (4B).

questions.q: Which of the following is a factor that contributes to a successful review?
o: Split large work products into smaller parts
Set reviewer evaluation as an objective
Plan to cover one document per review
questions.e: Splitting the work product into parts small enough to review in a reasonable time keeps reviewers focused. Management support is useful but participation is not required, and reviews must not evaluate the participants.

questions.q: What is the MAIN difference between black-box test techniques and experience-based test techniques?
o: The test level at which the test technique is used
The software development lifecycle (SDLC) in which the test technique can be used
questions.e: Black-box techniques derive tests from the specified behaviour, so the test basis is a specification, while experience-based techniques rely on the tester's knowledge and experience and may not use the specification at all. Both work on the same test objects, at all levels and in all lifecycles.

questions.q:
You are testing a PIN validator which accepts valid and rejects invalid PINs. A PIN is valid if it consists of four digits which are not all the same digit. Valid equivalence partitions identified:
Variable PIN code length: 'length correct' (four-digit PINs), 'length incorrect' (PINs with length other than 4).
Variable number of different digits: 'number of different digits correct' (at least two different digits), 'number of different digits incorrect' (all digits the same).
Which of the following is the BEST set of input test data to cover the partitions?
questions.e: 12 covers 'too few digits', 1111 covers 'length correct' with all digits the same, 1234 covers 'length correct' with different digits, and 12345 covers 'too many digits', so every partition is covered. Option b only tests the short side, c has no valid PIN, and d misses the 'all digits the same' partition.

questions.q:
A business rule is: INPUT: value (integer). IF (value <= 100 OR value >= 200) THEN write 'value incorrect' ELSE write 'value OK'.
You design test cases using 2-value boundary value analysis. Which set of test inputs achieves the greatest coverage?
questions.e: The boundary values are 100, 101, 199 and 200. Option d exercises three of those four coverage items (101, 199, 200), while each other option reaches only two, that is 50%.

questions.q:
A decision table for driving test results has three rules:
R1: theoretical exam passed T, practical exam passed T -> issue a driving license
R2: theoretical exam passed F -> request additional driving lessons
R3: first attempt at the exam F, practical exam passed F -> request to take the exam again.
What test data will show that there are contradictory rules in the decision table?
o: C1 = T, C2 = T, C3 = F
C1 = T, C2 = F, C3 = T
C1 = T, C2 = T, C3 = T and C1 = F, C2 = T, C3 = T
C1 = F, C2 = F, C3 = F
questions.e: The combination C1 = F, C2 = F, C3 = F satisfies both R2 and R3, which ask for different actions, so it proves the rules contradict each other. The other combinations match a single rule or none at all.

questions.q:
You are designing test cases based on a state transition diagram for a hotel room reservation system with the states START, REQUESTING, WAITING LIST, CONFIRMED and END. Transitions: START -Room request-> REQUESTING; REQUESTING -Available-> CONFIRMED; REQUESTING -Not available-> WAITING LIST; WAITING LIST -Available-> CONFIRMED; WAITING LIST -Cancel-> END; CONFIRMED -Pay-> END.
What is the MINIMUM number of test cases required to achieve 100% valid transitions coverage?
questions.e: The transitions REQUESTING to CONFIRMED, WAITING LIST to CONFIRMED and WAITING LIST to END cannot all occur in one test case, which forces at least three cases: Room request-Available-Pay; Room request-Not available-Available-Pay; Room request-Not available-Cancel.

questions.q: You want to apply branch testing to the code represented by a control flow graph that contains 7 nodes and 8 edges. How many coverage items do you need to test?
questions.e: In branch testing the coverage items are branches, which are the edges of the control flow graph, so 8 edges means 8 coverage items. Nodes are not coverage items for branch testing.

questions.q: How can white-box testing be useful in support of black-box testing?
o: White-box coverage measures can help testers evaluate black-box tests in terms of the code coverage achieved by these black-box tests
White-box coverage analysis can help testers identify unreachable fragments of the source code
Branch testing subsumes black-box test techniques, so achieving full branch coverage guarantees achieving full coverage of any black-box technique
White-box test techniques can provide coverage items for black-box techniques
questions.e: Black-box testing alone gives no measure of code coverage, so white-box coverage measures show how much code the black-box tests actually reached and where more tests are needed. Option b is true but unrelated to supporting black-box testing, and white-box and black-box coverage items are unrelated.

questions.q: Consider the following list: correct input not accepted; incorrect input accepted; wrong output format; division by zero. What test technique is MOST PROBABLY used by the tester who uses this list when performing testing?
questions.e: A list of possible errors, defects and failures that guides test design is a fault attack, the methodical form of error guessing. A checklist would hold test conditions rather than failures, and BVA needs partitions and boundaries.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes how using checklist-based testing can result in increased coverage?
o: Checklist items can be defined at a sufficiently low level of detail, so the tester can implement and execute detailed test cases based on these items
Checklists can be automated, so each time an automated test execution covers the checklist items, it results in additional coverage
Each checklist item should be tested separately and independently, so the elements cover different areas of the software
Two testers designing and executing tests based on the same high-level checklist items will typically perform the testing in slightly different ways
questions.e: High-level checklists leave room for variation, so two testers using the same items will explore slightly different areas and together cover more, at the cost of repeatability. Automation and independent item testing do not increase coverage.

questions.q: Which of the following provides the BEST example of a scenario-oriented acceptance criterion?
o: The application must allow users to delete their account and all associated data upon request
When a customer adds an item to their cart and proceeds to checkout, they should be prompted to log in or create an account if they haven't already done so
The website must comply with the ICT Accessibility 508 Standards and ensure that all content is accessible to users with disabilities
questions.e: Option b describes an example scenario the system must realise. Options a and d are rule-oriented, and option c is written like code, which business stakeholders cannot read.

questions.q:
You use acceptance test-driven development on the user story: As a Regular or Special user, I want to be able to use my electronic floor card, to access specific floors. Acceptance criteria: AC1 Regular users have access to floors 1 to 3; AC2 Floor 4 is only accessible to Special users; AC3 Special users have all the access rights of Regular users.
Which test case is the MOST reasonable one to test AC3?
o: Check that a Regular user can access floors 1 and 3
Check that a Regular user cannot access floor 4
Check that a Special user can access floor 5
Check that a Special user can access floors 1, 2 and 3
questions.e: AC3 says Special users inherit the rights of Regular users, so the test must show a Special user reaching floors 1, 2 and 3. Options a and b test Regular users, and floor 5 is outside the acceptance criteria.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of a test plan?
o: To define test data and expected results for component tests and component integration tests
To define as exit criteria from the component test level that '100% statement coverage and 100% branch coverage must be achieved'
To describe what fields the test progress report shall contain and what should be the form of this report
To explain why system integration testing will be excluded from testing, although the test strategy requires this test level
questions.e: A test plan may state test data requirements but never the detailed test data and expected results of individual test cases, which belong to the test cases themselves. Entry and exit criteria, report templates and justified deviations from the strategy are all valid test plan content.

questions.q:
At the start of each iteration the team estimates the work in person-days. Let E(n) be the estimate for iteration n and A(n) the actual work done in iteration n. From iteration 3 the team uses E(n) = (3*A(n-1) + A(n-2)) / 4. The graph of estimates and actuals shows A(3) = 8 and A(4) = 6 person-days.
What is the estimated amount of work for iteration 5?
questions.e: Using the formula: E(5) = (3*A(4) + A(3)) / 4 = (3*6 + 8) / 4 = 26 / 4 = 6.5 person-days.

questions.q:
You prepare a test execution schedule for test cases TC1 to TC7 with priorities (1 highest, 3 lowest) and dependencies given by arrows, where an arrow from TC4 to TC7 means TC7 can only run after TC4. The priority 1 test cases are TC5 and TC7, priority 2 are TC1, TC3 and TC4, and priority 3 are TC2 and TC6. TC7 depends on TC4; TC5 depends on TC4 and TC2; TC2 depends on TC1.
Which test case should be executed sixth?
questions.e: Respecting both priority and dependencies, the schedule is TC4, TC7, TC1, TC2, TC5, TC3, TC6, so TC3 is sixth and the lowest priority case TC6 runs last.

questions.q: What does the test pyramid model show?
o: That tests may have different priorities
That tests may have different granularity
That tests may require different coverage criteria
That tests may depend on other tests
questions.e: The test pyramid shows that tests have different levels of granularity, with many fine-grained tests at the bottom and few broad tests at the top. It says nothing about priorities, coverage criteria or dependencies.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the testing quadrants, test levels and test types?
o: Testing quadrants represent particular combinations of test levels and test types, defining their location in the software development lifecycle
Testing quadrants describe the degree of granularity of individual test types performed at each test level
Testing quadrants assign the test types that can be performed to the test levels
Testing quadrants group test levels and test types by several criteria such as targeting specific stakeholders
questions.e: The quadrants group test levels, test types, activities, techniques and work products by whether they are business or technology facing and whether they support the team or critique the product. The degree of granularity is what the test pyramid describes.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of how product risk analysis may influence the thoroughness and scope of testing?
o: Continuous risk monitoring allows us to identify an emerging risk as soon as possible
Risk identification allows us to implement risk mitigation activities and reduce the risk level
The assessed risk level helps us to select the rigor of testing
Risk analysis allows us to derive coverage items
questions.e: The assessed risk level determines how rigorously and how broadly the related areas are tested, which is exactly the influence of risk analysis on thoroughness and scope. Monitoring and mitigation belong to risk control, and coverage items come from test techniques.

questions.q: Which of the following activities in the test process makes the MOST use of test progress reports?
questions.e: The test completion report is built from the information in test progress reports, which are mainly produced during monitoring and control and used again at completion. Analysis, design and planning do not consume progress reports.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of how configuration management supports testing?
o: All commits to the repository are uniquely identified and version controlled
All changes in the test environment elements are tracked
All requirement specifications are referenced unambiguously in test plans
All identified defects have an assigned status
questions.e: Giving defects a status is the job of defect management, not configuration management. Unique commit identification, tracked environment changes and unambiguous references in test documentation are all configuration management tasks.

questions.q:
A defect report for a web-based shopping application states: Application WebShop v0.99; defect: login button not working; steps: launch the website, click the login button; expected: the user is redirected to the login page; actual: the login button does not respond when clicked; severity high; priority urgent.
What is the MOST important information that is missing from this defect report?
o: Name of the tester and date
Test environment elements and their version numbers
Impact on the interests of stakeholders
questions.e: The browser and device or other environment elements are missing, and this kind of defect is often environment specific, so the developers may not reproduce it. The test object (WebShop v0.99) and the impact (severity high) are present.

questions.q: Tools from which of the following categories help with the organization of test cases, detected defects and configuration management?
questions.e: Test management tools facilitate management of the SDLC, requirements, tests, defects and configuration management. Execution, design and defect tools each cover only one narrow area.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a benefit of test automation?
o: The capability of generating test cases without access to the test basis
The achievement of increased coverage through more objective assessment
The increase in test execution times available with higher processing power
The prevention of human errors through greater consistency and repeatability
questions.e: Tools apply the same tests, data and order consistently every time, which prevents human error. Test cases still need a test basis, objective coverage measurement alone does not raise coverage, and higher processing power shortens execution.
